devices.role: recording rig for the committed client-performance baseline (run-2026-09-03 and results-2026-09-04)
devices.note: desktop Chromium on the actual recording machine, unthrottled; not a physical mobile device. Physical-device rows replace or extend this scope at qualification time.

note: Real measured p95 budgets, recorded on the lab rig (MacBook-Pro.local, 18 x Apple M5 Pro, Chromium 151.0.7922.34, the unthrottled mainstream-desktop tier is the actual recording machine) at the real challenge configurations: Argon2id at the adaptive-risk ladder (m=16384 KiB, t=3, p=1, target 8), the rsw time-lock rungs at T=75,000 / 150,000 / 300,000 squarings (the default rung, the midpoint and the protocol ceiling of 10,000..=300,000), SHA-256 at 16/18/20 bits, and the ExecutionChallengeV1 cells (the files-tier execvm/execsha18/execargon/execchain and the inline-tier execvminline/execsha18inline). Every row is ceil(1.2 x merged p95) of the measurements in tools/client-perf/results/baseline.json: the p95 is the worst asset mode of the cell merged across the inline and files repetitions (the harness percentile semantics over the concatenated samples), and the fixed 20% margin is the documented allowance for the CDP-emulation noise this lab itself measures, not a placeholder factor. Evidence runs: results/run-2026-09-03.json (desktop real-ladder run, 12 SHA / 6 Argon reps per mode) and tools/client-perf/results/results-2026-09-04.json (focused run, 50 reps, the rsw rungs and the inline execution cells). The qualified tier scope is mainstream-desktop only: it is the tier that represents the actual lab hardware. The five emulation tiers (low-android, mid-android, flagship-android, older-iphone, current-iphone) and low-desktop carry no budget rows because no real-ladder qualification evidence exists for them; emulation tiers are calibration signals, never release boundaries. The release-gate procedure (physical-device qualification replacing this file tier by tier) is documented in tools/client-perf/README.md. maxCellFailureRate 0.05 reflects the measured 1-in-24 exhaustion tail of the sha20 warm files-mode cell (a 20-bit pure-JS search can exhaust the 5M-hash cap); 0.02 would reject the lab's own completed evidence.
